title: Diablo
designer: David Brevik, Erich Schaefer, Max Schaefer
shortDescription: Blizzard North's dark fantasy action RPG that revitalized the genre with procedural dungeons, addictive loot drops, and Battle.net.
historicalSignificance: Transformed slow turn-based Roguelikes into an adrenaline-fueled real-time action RPG loop of clicking, loot drops, and dungeon crawling, supported by Blizzard's free Battle.net online matchmaker.

editorialContent.overview: Developed by Blizzard North (originally Condor Inc.) and released on the eve of 1997, Diablo resurrected the Western role-playing game from commercial slumber. Conceived by David Brevik as a stop-motion claymation turn-based roguelike, Blizzard convinced the team to pivot to real-time action, producing one of the most addictive feedback loops in computing history under the cursed cathedral of Tristram.
editorialContent.gameplay: Choosing between Warrior, Rogue, and Sorcerer, players descend through sixteen procedurally generated dungeon tiers leading to Hell itself. Gameplay is built upon mouse-driven tactical positioning, potion management, spell casting, and an irresistible random loot generator offering prefix/suffix magical equipment.
editorialContent.technicalInnovation: Pioneered real-time SVGA isometric sprite rendering combined with server-synchronized multiplayer on Battle.net, enabling players across the globe to team up for cooperative dungeon clearing at zero subscription cost.
editorialContent.culturalImpact: Matt Uelmen's iconic 12-string acoustic Tristram guitar theme became immortal, and Diablo's color-coded loot tier hierarchy (White, Blue, Gold) became the foundational economy for the modern gaming industry, from World of Warcraft to Destiny and Borderlands.
editorialContent.preservationNotes: Preserved through community source reimplementations (DevilutionX), GOG digital releases, and original retail CD-ROM archives.

awards: Computer Gaming World Game of the Year 1996
Origins Award Best Roleplaying Computer Game 1996

technicalSpecs.engine: Blizzard North SVGA isometric 2D sprite engine
technicalSpecs.soundChip: DirectSound / Miles Sound System wavetable audio
